Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~76 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Hannah Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Luis Gomez (Redwood SE), Ellen Brooks (Cedarloop Head of ML), Devon Ortiz (Platform Eng), Asha Malik (Security), Tom Reeves (Product), Nadia (notes)

Samir: quick overview of pilot and timeline; Ellen: current infra and constraints; Hannah: perf and staging plan; Asha: security asks; Devon: networking constraints.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll run through the ramp plan and make sure the staging checklist maps to your infra. quick intro — i'm Samir from Redwood.
[00:15] Ellen: hi hi, Ellen here. quick note, we've got a clinical search product, short latency is important for triage — 200 to 400ms ideal for single-turn responses.
[00:30] Devon: Devon — we run on AWS in us-west-2, private subnets, strict egress control, and we need VPC peering or PrivateLink, not open internet.
[00:44] Asha: Asha, security — SOC2 in progress, keys in our KMS, we can't hand over keys. looking for CMKs via cross-account or HSM integration.
[00:58] Hannah: okay noted, on Redwood Private we support customer-managed KMS and bring-your-own-key patterns; for the pilot we can do an isolated Dedicated pool w/ VPC peering — we'll outline options.
[01:15] Tom: timeline question: how quickly can we move from staging to pilot? we want production in ~6 weeks.
[01:25] Priya: 6 weeks is feasible for a focused pilot; typical cadence is: week 0 staging and connectivity, week 1 sample evals, weeks 2-4 load tests & tuning, final week for go/no-go and rollouts.
[01:40] Ellen: that works but we need to confirm cost envelope — are we locked into a big reserve for Dedicated?
[01:50] Samir: good question — for pilots we usually offer a limited-duration dedicated pool with lower commit; we'll include a pilot pricing tier in SOW. not full reserved capacity.
[02:05] Devon: one thing — our platform uses strict CIDR ranges; we need the exact egress IPs and ranges for the staging job.
[02:16] Luis: we'll provide the IP ranges; for Dedicated we can also do VPC peering which avoids public egress, so less friction.
[02:28] Asha: about audit logs — we need long-term access to invocation logs for compliance and will need to verify log retention and redaction.
[02:40] Priya: Redwood Console supports token-level tracing and per-route logs; we'll map retention to your requirements and redact PII as needed. we'll share the retention matrix.
[02:55] Ellen: any limitations with quantized models on medical text? we've seen hallucinations on small quantized variants.
[03:06] Hannah: yes context — quantization can change model calibration. for the pilot we'll run both a 4-bit quantized variant and FP16 baseline on a sample prompt set to compare QA/regression. we'll set up quality monitors.
[03:25] Samir: action — Hannah will run a short quality comparison on the sample prompts, with the KV cache warming to match production patterns.
[04:05] [small cross talk, background noise]
[04:40] Ellen: also, data residency — do you store prompts or just pass-through? we have to know exactly what is persisted.
[04:52] Samir: by default hosted logs are retained for X days for debugging, but we can opt for no retention and ship logs to your S3 via customer-managed retention; for Dedicated/Private you retain control. we'll include options in the SOW.
[05:20] Devon: scoring — throughput? our peak is 120 qps with 100 token avg, but most traffic is bursty.
[05:33] Hannah: okay we'll look at autoscale policies and cost-aware batching; for latency-sensitive short responses we'll tune batching thresholds to favor latency over throughput.
[06:00] Tom: can we get RBAC scoped to teams? we want product people to see metrics but not raw logs.
[06:10] Priya: yes RBAC is supported via SSO and role groups; SAML will be integrated. we'll share the RBAC mapping guide.
[06:30] Asha: regarding SAML, we need metadata exchange and test pre-prod assertion flow.
[06:40] Samir: noted; Priya will set up a short runbook for SAML test steps.
[07:00] [10 minute jump, discussing staging benchmarks]
[17:05] Hannah: plan for the staging benchmark: we'll use your sample dataset (Ellen to provide 5k short queries + 500 long queries), run 3 runs for each model variant, capture p50/p95 latency, token cost, and quality metrics (exact-match / rouge / domain eval).
[17:30] Ellen: I'll export and share artifacts to the shared drive by Friday.
[17:40] Devon: any infra changes needed from our side? we prefer VPC peering but we can tolerate NAT egress if necessary for a fast test.
[18:00] Luis: NAT egress will work for initial smoke tests but for the full benchmark we recommend peering to avoid throttling and latency variability.
[18:20] Asha: encryption at rest — keys are managed in our KMS. we want to confirm how snapshots/backups are handled.
[18:30] Hannah: for Dedicated snapshots we can configure encryption using your CMK and ensure backups are in your account. we'll capture the exact flow in the security docs.
[18:50] Samir: competitor question — Ellen, you mentioned Anthropic earlier; are you evaluating them in parallel?
[19:00] Ellen: yes a small eval, plus another vendor called Megacorp AI. cost and latency are primary comparators.
[19:12] Samir: got it. we'll highlight where Redwood offers predictable latency and batching controls.
[19:30] [noise — someone's phone]
[21:00] Tom: what happens if the pilot exceeds the cost envelope? do you support automatic throttle or fallbacks?
[21:12] Priya: we can set per-route quotas and automatic fallback policies to smaller model variants; Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization configs to reduce unit cost.
[21:40] Devon: on monitoring — what metrics will you push to our monitoring stack?
[21:50] Luis: we can export traces and metrics via Prometheus pushgateway or a pull endpoint; we'll share the exporter config.
[22:05] Ellen: alerting — we need email + pager for P95 > 1s and error rate > 2%.
[22:20] Priya: we'll map alerts and handoffs; also include a runbook for on-call.
[22:40] [silence, people reviewing docs]
[28:00] Hannah: technical deep dive note: KV cache warmup — if you often do multi-turn, cache affinity helps latency significantly; we'll show you the cache-hit curves in the benchmark.
[28:25] Ellen: multi-turn is occasional but important; we'll want to see the difference.
[28:40] Samir: Okay recapping — deliverables: SOW & pilot pricing, IP ranges for peering, SAML metadata, sample dataset, staging benchmark plan.
[29:00] Ellen: timeline again — we aim to start staging by 9/20. is that realistic?
[29:12] Hannah: yes if networking and KMS metadata are exchanged this week. we'll provision a dedicated pool for the pilot the week of 9/20.
[29:30] Devon: I'll try to get the peering request in by EOD Monday.
[29:40] Asha: i'll send KMS policy snippets and required roles.
[30:05] Samir: perfect. pricing and SOW will come from me by Thursday (9/17).
[30:30] [mid-call clarifying questions about the SOW specifics]
[40:00] Luis: question about data retention for logs — if we ship logs to Cedarloop S3, how fast can we query them?
[40:10] Priya: querying is up to your analytics stack; we can index logs before shipping, or ship raw and you run Athena/Glue. we'll propose both options.
[40:30] Ellen: for auditing we want exports for a rolling 13 months.
[40:40] Asha: retention and export formats are critical for our auditors.
[41:00] Hannah: noted — we'll include a retention & export appendix in the security pack.
[41:20] [people discussing small implementation detail: tenant mapping & namespaces]
[50:00] Devon: one more thing — how do we map product tenants to Redwood tokens and costs? we want per-tenant billing.
[50:20] Samir: Redwood Console supports token-level cost breakdown by route/model and you can map tokens to tenant IDs; we'll send a sample export for billing integration.
[50:40] Tom: great.
[55:00] [wrap-up, next steps readout]
[55:10] Samir: recapping next steps — i'll send SOW and pilot pricing; Hannah runs staging perf; Priya and Asha will handle SAML/KMS and retention; Devon shares peering info; Ellen shares sample dataset.
[55:30] Ellen: all good. any blockers on Redwood side?
[55:40] Hannah: none — we have the capacity; just need the networking metadata.
[55:50] Priya: i'll schedule a 1-hr staging runbook call for 9/20 to line up engineers.
[56:05] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and attach the security pack and SOW.
[56:20] Tom: thanks.
[56:30] [meeting ends, casual goodbyes]
[01:16:00] [call disconnected]
